candidates.changed_node: numerator anchor $close -> $open, with TS_MIN($low, 21) -> TS_MIN($low, 5) in both places
candidates.rationale: Weakest component: the numerator's $close. $close is the ADJUSTED close while $high/$low are raw, so $close - TS_MIN($low,21) is dominated by the cumulative dividend-adjustment ratio, which depends on dividends paid after the observation date. That ratio shrinks toward the end of the panel, which is exactly the monotone IC decay (0.0250 in 2000 to 0.0010 in 2013) - the decay is the lookahead draining, not a regime. Re-anchor on the raw $open so numerator and denominator live on one price scale, and shorten the floor to 5 days because the honest residual signal is short-horizon reversal, not 21-day position. The denominator's floor window moves with the numerator's only because ($close - TS_MIN($low,21)) and (TS_MAX($high,21) - TS_MIN($low,21)) are both archived blocks at 5 and 7 nodes.

Weakest component: the reversal leg TS_SUM($return, 5). IC half-life is 4.3 days against 0.204 one-way turnover - the leg decays faster than the position is held, so it pays the batch's largest cost for signal that is gone by the time it is traded. The $roa leg is slow and fine. Widen the window to 21 days to match decay to holding period, and keep only the downside (MIN($return,0)), where the short-horizon reversal premium actually persists; 2012, the one negative year, was a low-volatility grind in which the signed 5-day sum is noise. RANK(TS_SUM($return,21)) alone was already tried on another island and came back at |rho| 0.814, so the asymmetry is doing the decorrelating as well as the diagnostic work.

candidates.changed_node: TS_CORR window 15 -> 63, with the lead level $roe -> $asset_turnover
candidates.rationale: Weakest component: the 15-day TS_CORR window. Fifteen observations put the standard error of a correlation estimate near 0.27, so the leg is mostly estimation noise, which is why the factor turns negative in 2003 and why its IC (0.01068) is below the 42-day sibling's (0.01127) despite a shorter half-life. Sixty-three days quadruples the estimation sample and keeps the range-vs-volume kernel that carries this island's best accepts. The lead has to move with it: CS_RANK(TS_CORR($volume,$high-$low,15)) is a 7-node archived block, and CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) is the prefix that pins rho for this whole family, so the profitability level moves to a different accounting dimension ($asset_turnover), not to $roa.

Weakest component: the MAX(TS_DELTA($leverage,63), 0) gate. $leverage is the sparsest field in the expression and drags coverage to 0.964, the lowest of the batch, while buying almost nothing - the same factor without the gate (the 15-day sibling) posts 0.01068 IC against this one's 0.01127, and the gate is what spends the fifth field, the only free constant and 0.200 of fitness. Every wrapper of TS_DELTA($leverage,63) is already an archived 4-node block. Replace it with the dense $asset_turnover trend, which keeps the one-sided fundamental-improvement gate and buys back coverage. The lead and the correlation's range leg move with it because both of the parent's remaining blocks are archived whole.

Weakest component: the normaliser $dollar_volume / ($open + 1e-8). $dollar_volume is stored as raw close times volume, so dividing by $open just recovers share volume - and TS_CORR is scale-invariant, so the division does no work at all. The leg is therefore a 63-day restatement of the plain volume-versus-range correlation, which is precisely why this factor sits at |rho| 0.794 against the archive's 42-day version of exactly that and why it repeats the family's 2003 negative (-0.0086, the worst here). Dividing dollar volume by its own 21-day mean is the one substitution that changes the series' shape inside the window rather than its scale: the leg becomes relative turnover, so the correlation measures whether volume surprises accompany range expansion.

Weakest component: the raw $volume level. Stability is 0.86, the worst in the batch, with 2003 and 2013 both negative. A 21-day correlation taken against a level that trends - share volume grows through the sample and jumps discontinuously at splits, unlike $dollar_volume - measures the co-trend rather than the volume-volatility relation, and the sign of that co-trend is what flips between regimes. TS_RANK over 63 days detrends volume within each name and bounds it, leaving the range-versus-volume kernel (this island's strongest) untouched. Deliberately 63 rather than the archived 10-day rank, so this is not a restatement of the existing TS_RANK($volume,10)/42-day member.

Weakest component: TS_DELTA($dollar_volume, 5) inside a 21-day correlation. IC half-life is 4.7 days, five times shorter than the 21-day sibling's, at higher turnover (0.122). An unbounded 5-day difference of a dollar-volume level is set by one or two spike days, so the 21-day correlation is effectively estimated off a handful of observations and has nothing left to say by the end of the week. TS_RANK keeps the same 5-day volume-surprise idea but bounds it, and the 63-day correlation window gives the estimate three times the sample. Both edits attack the one named weakness; the 21-day TS_DELTA variant of this expression is already archived, so a window-only edit was not available.

Weakest component: the numerator TS_MEAN($high - $low, 10). IC half-life 57.1 days at 0.029 turnover says this leg is a near-static characteristic - a normalised range level is a volatility ranking that barely moves month to month, so it tilts the roe leg by beta rather than by anything dated. Replacing the mean with the standard deviation of the same range turns a level into range instability, which varies at the horizon the factor is actually traded at, and lengthening the price denominator to 63 days stops the scaler co-moving with the numerator (both were 10-day means of overlapping windows). The lead moves to $roa only because TS_MEAN($high-$low,10) and TS_MEAN($open,10)+1e-8 are both archived 5-node blocks; the decorrelation has to come from the mean-to-std change, not from the field swap.

Weakest component: the price scaler TS_MAX($high, 21) / ($open + 1e-8). It sits in a narrow band near 1.0 to 1.2 for every name, so multiplying the leverage delta by it barely reorders anything - it spends two of the five fields and 0.200 of fitness to do nothing. The direct evidence: a 126-day version of the same scaler came back at |rho| 0.920 against this parent, i.e. the scaler is not what the factor is measuring. TS_STD($high,21) over $open is the same two raw-scale fields expressed as a dispersion that genuinely varies cross-sectionally, so the leverage delta gets modulated by volatility instead of by a constant. The lead wrapper becomes CS_ZSCORE only because CS_RANK($roa - $accrual_gap) is an archived 4-node block.

candidates.changed_node: TS_RANK($close, 168) -> TS_RANK($close, 126), with the lead delta field $roa -> $asset_turnover
candidates.rationale: Weakest component: the 168-day window on TS_RANK($close). Coverage is 0.912, the tightest in the batch and one constraint away from the 0.90 gate, and the 168-day price rank is what buys it - eight months of price history stacked on top of a 63-day fundamental delta. This island's coverage evidence puts the break just above 168 days and shows 126-day price extrema sitting inside accepts, so 126 keeps the medium-horizon momentum content the leg contributes (it is the multiplicative TS_RANK placement that earned this factor its fitness) while returning headroom. The lead field moves to $asset_turnover because CS_ZSCORE(TS_DELTA($roa,63)) is an archived 4-node block and asset_turnover is equally dense, so coverage does not pay for the swap.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.
